title: Go runtime frontier marking versus the materialised Soufflé closure of the pointer graph joined with the roots
explanation: Two distinct Datalog programs are involved: a unary marking program Marked(x) :- RootPtr(x); Marked(y) :- Marked(x), HeapPtr(x,y), and Soufflé's benchmark transitive-closure program Tc(x,y) :- HeapPtr(x,y); Tc(x,z) :- Tc(x,y), Tc(y,z) over the same pointer-graph edges HeapPtr. Side 1 encodes the Go runtime's garbage-collector marking (gcDrain/scanObject/greyobject): a worklist ('grey set') traversal that starts at the roots and, level by level, marks and enqueues every newly reached object, stopping when the queue is empty. Side 2 is the non-linear (doubling) naive fixpoint computation of Tc, the full pointer-graph reachability closure, independent of any roots. The Hoare triple links the two different schemas by a view stated in the postcondition: it claims the GC's marked set equals the roots together with everything the materialized closure Tc says is reachable from some root — i.e. that frontier-by-frontier marking from the roots computes exactly the root-restricted transitive closure of the pointer graph.
preInWords: The precondition is simply true; no constraints are placed on RootPtr or HeapPtr.
postInWords: Marked, the set produced by the GC's root-seeded frontier marking traversal, equals RootPtr unioned with the objects reachable from some root according to the separately computed pointer-graph transitive closure Tc.
family: production algorithm pair (dependent phases, schema link by view)
obstructionExpectation: rate mismatch (one pointer per round versus path-length doubling) with the join applied to the finished closure; leveled-framework target; with prophecy the non-linear fixpoint equation gives transitivity, so both containments follow from the fixpoint facts
sides: hand-written: Go gcDrain/scanObject/greyobject frontier marking (legacy Example2012 program)
naive compiler: Soufflé tc (non-linear closure of HeapPtr), joined with RootPtr in the postcondition
schemaLinking: the unary marked set and the binary closure are linked by the view Marked = RootPtr ∪ π[2](σ[#0 = #1](RootPtr × Tc)) stated as the postcondition (method 3 of the handoff)
